text:
Colorado had 78 shot attempts to Toronto's 43 and out-chanced them 4.64 to 3.07 in expected goals, yet lost 6-3. Run every shot through a thousand simulated replays and the Avalanche win 84 percent of them. This was the other 17 percent, give or take, and it hinged on a 45-second stretch late in the second period.

Colorado led 3-2 after Brock Nelson's goal, and the period had been theirs: 2.09 expected goals to Toronto's 0.61. Then William Nylander tied it at 16:47 with a wrist shot that carried a 12 percent chance of going in, and Easton Cowan answered the next faceoff cycle at 17:33 with a slap shot that was worth just 8 percent. Two low-quality looks, two goals, and Toronto walked into the room up 4-3. Nylander, the game's first star, finished with two goals and three assists, and he set up Cowan as well. Nathan MacKinnon scored twice for Colorado on 8 shots, both goals from chances worth 7 and 6 percent.

Sergei Bobrovsky did the quiet work, facing shot quality that should have cost Toronto 4.64 goals and allowing three, about 1.6 better than expected. Mackenzie Blackwood went the other way, allowing five on shots worth 2.23, nearly three goals worse than expected. Toronto's power play went 2 for 4 while Colorado's went 0 for 5, and Auston Matthews put it away with a power-play goal at 12:02 of the third and an empty-netter at 19:21 for the 6-3 final.
